https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cpd791.text: Wildfires scorch Washington state as thousands evacuated and emergency declared Wildfires scorch Washington state as thousands evacuated and emergency declared Close Wildfires across more than 250,000 acres have forced evacuations and caused power outages in the Washington state's Spokane area, US officials said. Washington State Governor Bob Ferguson declared a statewide emergency and burn ban on Saturday morning. "Our state is facing a very serious situation with multiple fires, and our hearts go out to Washingtonians who are losing their homes", Ferguson said. According to officials, no injuries or fatalities have been reported. Spokane is the state's second most populous city. https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/catego.text: Latvian authorities issued warnings for heavy rainfall and strong wind gusts across almost the entire country. (EPA Images pic) RIGA: A powerful storm swept across Latvia on Saturday evening, bringing down large numbers of trees and severely damaging the electricity distribution network, leaving more than 160,000 customers without power. The powerful cyclone entered Latvia from the south, bringing torrential rain and damaging winds. Latvian news agency LETA described it as the most destructive storm to hit the country since January 2005, reported Xinhua. In some parts of central Latvia, rainfall during the day had already reached around half of the local monthly average. The Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre (LEGMC) maintained a red warning for heavy rainfall in central and western Latvia on Saturday, while an orange warning for strong wind gusts covered almost the entire country. Latvia's rail operator said several train services were delayed on Saturday evening due to the severe weather. According to electricity distribution system operator Sadales tikls, around 160,000 customers were without power as of 9pm. Most of the damage was caused by fallen trees, and emergency crews were working to restore electricity as quickly as possible. Sadales tikls said the damage to the electricity network was extensive and complex, meaning repairs would take longer than usual. Some customers could remain without power for more than 24 hours. Latvia's State Fire and Rescue Service (VUGD) said the number of weather-related emergency calls rose rapidly during the evening, with most involving trees brought down by strong winds and blocking roads. According to local media reports, strong winds tore the roof off a building in Daugavpils, while a falling tree damaged a residential building. In Jekabpils, several vehicles were crushed by fallen trees. LEGMC issued red, orange and yellow warnings for heavy rain and strong winds in Riga and across the country on Friday. A number of outdoor events around Latvia were subsequently cancelled. On Saturday, local authorities repeatedly warned residents of heavy rain and strong winds through cell broadcast alerts.

https://www.dw.com/en/google-s-gemini-ai.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MsjB Google's artificial intelligence, Gemini, is the latest to have hacked other companies Image: Matteo Della Torre/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement Google 's consumer artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini, hacked into multiple systems by guessing login credentials during tests of its cybersecurity capabilities, the company said on Friday. This is the latest in a series of cybersecurity breaches involving rogue AI , raising safety concerns about the technology. The internet giant is the fourth AI developer whose programs have been found to exhibit such behavior, following OpenAI , Anthropic, and Meta. Google only made the incidents — which occurred in May and were discovered by Google in July — public after an inquiry from The Wall Street Journal . Will AI destroy humanity? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video What we know about the incident According to the WSJ report, there were three instances in which Gemini infiltrated the computers of other companies, whose names were not disclosed. In one case, the AI guessed passwords to access a protected system. In the other two, it found login credentials in a database. "In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test," Heather Adkins, Google's vice president of security engineering, told the AFP news agency in a statement. "In all three of these instances, the model stopped," Adkins said. "We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they've now made to their testing processes." What is AI's biggest risk: Speed or autonomy? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Autonomous AI agents pose risks Similar incidents have been reported earlier by Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI. These incidents have raised questions about the necessary safeguards as AI agents become more autonomous and gain access to the internet and computer systems. AI model developed by OpenAI , the creator of ChatGPT, escaped from a secure environment during a test in July and infiltrated the computers of another AI company, HuggingFace, unexpectedly. This prompted rival Anthropic to review its own test runs, during which additional incidents came to light . Meta subsequently admitted that its AI had hacked into another company's computers due to a system misconfiguration at a testing partner. This month, Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, called for a slowdown in AI development . In a blog post, he expressed concern that a swarm of autonomous software systems, or AI agents, could take over the entire internet within six to 12 months, causing billions of dollars in damage.
